summary: Extends ACME so certificate authorities can issue certificates for IP addresses, not just domain names. It defines a new identifier type for IP addresses and a challenge that lets a client show it controls the address in question.

plainLanguage.summary: Normally a certificate says a name belongs to someone. This lets the certificate be about a numbered address instead, once the owner proves the address is theirs.

questions: how to get a certificate for an ip address
does acme support ip address identifiers
which acme challenges work for ip addresses
subtitle: Lets ACME certificate authorities validate and issue certificates for IP addresses.

tldr.problem: ACME only defines challenges for validating control of DNS host names, so it could not be used to get certificates for IP addresses.
tldr.mechanism: A new identifier type "ip" is added, and the http-01 and tls-alpn-01 challenges are adapted to validate it, skipping DNS resolution and using the identifier's address.
tldr.outcome: Clients can prove control of an IPv4 or IPv6 address. The dns-01 challenge MUST NOT be used for IP identifiers.

today: RFC 8738 is a Proposed Standard and the metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: The IP Identifier
sections.content:
ACME (RFC 8555) defines only the identifier type dns. To request proof that a user controls an IPv4 or IPv6 address, an ACME server MUST create an authorization with the identifier type ip.

The value holds the textual form of the address, as in Section 2.1 of RFC 1123 for IPv4 and Section 4 of RFC 5952 for IPv6. For example: {"type": "ip", "value": "2001:db8::1"}.
sections.plainLanguage: Instead of saying "this name is mine", you can now say "this numbered address is mine".

sections.title: Validation Challenges
sections.content:
IP identifiers MAY be used with http-01 and with tls-alpn-01 (RFC 8737). For both, the initial DNS resolution step MUST be skipped, and the address used for validation MUST be the identifier's value.

For http-01, the Host header field MUST be set to the IP address being validated. For tls-alpn-01, the validation certificate's subjectAltName MUST contain a single iPAddress matching the address. Since SNI does not allow IP addresses in the HostName field, the server MUST use the IN-ADDR.ARPA or IP6.ARPA reverse mapping of the address as the HostName value.

The dns-01 challenge MUST NOT be used to validate IP identifiers.
sections.plainLanguage: You prove the address is yours by answering a visit made directly to that address. Checking a name's phone book entry is not allowed for this.

sections.title: IANA Registrations
sections.content: The label ip was added to the ACME Identifier Types registry. Two entries were added to the ACME Validation Methods registry: http-01 and tls-alpn-01, each with identifier type ip.
sections.plainLanguage: The official lists of ACME words got a new word, ip, and two existing checks were marked as working with it.

sections.title: Security and CA Policy
sections.content:
The extensions stay within the threat model of RFC 8555. The document only says how a server may validate that an applicant controls an IP identifier at the time of validation, and a CA may perform additional checks.

For example, if a CA believes an identifier belongs to an ISP or cloud provider with short delegation periods, it may impose additional restrictions on certificates for it.
sections.plainLanguage: Proving you hold an address today does not prove you will keep it, so a careful certificate issuer may ask for more checks.

cells: Yes, Host header set to the IP address
